A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SAFE-Pruner and provide readable text, equations, figures and tables. V1 includes Appendices A–D; the supplied v2 ends after the references. Their absence is an observable content difference, not an extraction gap.

before.justification: V1 reports original LIBERO, SIMPLER and real-robot evaluations, component ablations, and an attention-forecasting accuracy study in Appendix B.

after.justification: V2 retains original benchmark and ablation results, revises real-robot results, and adds a quantization compatibility experiment.

M1.justification: Token matching, saliency transfer, shallow/deep score fusion and threshold-triggered reference refresh remain unchanged in Eqs. (1)–(7). Adaptive selection already appears in v1 Section 3.4 and Algorithm 1, so replacing subtask terminology and removing fixed-interval wording does not establish an algorithm change. HiF8 is tested as a compatibility configuration.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same four LIBERO suites, SIMPLER Visual Matching and Variant Aggregation, and three Astribot manipulation tasks. Quantization changes the model configuration, while the removed forecasting study uses existing LIBERO coverage.

E2.justification: V2 Table 2 adds a comparison of SAFE-Pruner with SAFE-Pruner plus HiF8, alongside vanilla OpenVLA-OFT; HiF8 alone is not evaluated. Comparator membership in the existing LIBERO, SIMPLER and real-robot comparisons remains unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4.2 changes the reported real-robot evaluation from 20 to 200 trials per trained model, substantially expanding the stated evaluation sample. V2 also introduces a HiF8 configuration and GPU-memory metric. V1's separate 100-episode forecasting evaluation over timesteps 1–10 is removed. These reported changes do not establish which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 removes Appendix B's direct quantitative test of forecasting accuracy over time and Appendix C's pruning-ratio/pruning-layer complexity analysis. It adds quantization compatibility and memory analysis in Table 2. The component ablation remains, with 'w/o division' renamed 'w/o adaptivity' rather than replaced by a different ablation.

E5.justification: Removing Figure A also removes its mean±standard-deviation summaries: 0.957±0.013 for cosine similarity and 0.046±0.015 for KL divergence. V2 supplies no replacement uncertainty reporting; neither version reports confidence intervals or seed variability for the main success-rate tables.

E6.justification: V2 corrects the OpenVLA-OFT vanilla average from 97.0% to 96.8% in the main and ablation tables. Under the revised trial count, real-robot average success changes from 80.0/71.7/78.3% to 81.3/69.0/79.3% for vanilla/FastV/SAFE-Pruner, with revised latencies; these are not established same-protocol gains. New Table 2 reports 96.6% success, 1.729 T FLOPs and 11.03 GB memory for SAFE-Pruner plus HiF8. Appendix forecasting results disappear; SIMPLER scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: V2 removes Appendix C's supplementary FLOP derivation, including the per-layer cost C(N), full-model cost and pruned-model cost. The main mathematical definitions and pruning equations remain unchanged; no theorem or correctness proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract and contributions tighten the stated success-rate degradation from below 1.7% to below 1.5%. V2 withdraws the explicit 'first' discovery wording and changes 'fundamentally solving' short-sighted pruning to 'mitigating' it. Reference refresh replaces the claimed subtask-division contribution, while the central forecasting and acceleration claims remain.

C2.justification: V2 identifies accumulated forecasting drift as another reason to refresh references and interprets the threshold as detecting attention shifts rather than necessarily detecting subtask boundaries. It also qualifies accelerated models' superiority over vanilla as occurring only in some settings and adds an interpretation of complementary pruning and quantization benefits.

D1.justification: Removing Appendices A and D deletes concrete settings and implementation guidance: pruning at layer 3, the selected saliency layers, lambda=0.5, pruning ratios of 70–90%, gamma=0.92 for OpenVLA-OFT, and both pseudocode algorithms with vectorization details. V2 newly clarifies that latency includes key and non-key timesteps and all added overhead, but does not restore the missing implementation information.

R1.justification: V2 adds the HiFloat8 reference and removes RLRC. Section 3.2 newly credits VLA-Pruner and SpecPrune-VLA for adjacent-timestep attention overlap, positioning this work as extending that observation to longer horizons. Most related-work discussion is retained; citation renumbering and the pi0.5 author-name correction are not substantive changes.

P1.justification: The main section order and most prose remain intact. Local revisions standardize adaptive key-timestep terminology, clarify motivation and latency reporting, correct cross-references, and add contact information and acknowledgements. The appendices are omitted rather than reorganized into the main text.

P2.justification: The visual evidence changes substantially: v2 adds the quantization/memory table and removes appendix Figures A–B and Algorithms 1–2. Figure 4 receives revised reference-refresh labels, Table 1 corrects best-result highlighting, and the real-robot table is reformatted and relocated. Most main figures remain visually unchanged.

improvement.justification: V2 improves latency transparency, corrects averaging, reports a larger robot evaluation and adds quantization evidence. However, omitting Appendices A–D removes concrete reproduction settings and the direct quantitative validation of attention forecasting. These losses outweigh the additions to a limited extent, while the core method and most benchmark evidence remain intact.
